THE THREE FILES IN THIS FOLDER — the „Entfernen" tool of the photo window
=========================================================================

lama_small.onnx
    LaMa (big-lama), "Resolution-robust Large Mask Inpainting with Fourier
    Convolutions", Suvorov et al., Samsung AI Center, WACV 2022,
    https://github.com/advimman/lama — Apache License 2.0, trained on the
    Places2 data set. Converted to ONNX by Carve
    (https://huggingface.co/Carve/LaMa-ONNX, lama_fp32.onnx, 208 MB,
    Apache License 2.0).

    This copy was MADE HERE, not downloaded: the convolution weights of
    lama_fp32.onnx stored smaller. The large FFC convolutions (conv
    l2l/l2g/g2l and the 384x384 1x1, 170 MB of 204) blockwise as int8,
    each block of 64 values with its own scale — the procedure published
    with othytenk/lama-int4-int8 on Hugging Face, written anew; the rest
    (spectral transforms, down- and up-sampling, first and last layers)
    as half floats. The arithmetic stays fp32: onnxruntime folds the
    weights back once at load when the session sets
    session.disable_quant_qdq = 1. The script that made it stands below
    this text (mix.py). Inputs and outputs are the original's: image
    float32 [1,3,512,512] in 0..1, mask float32 [1,1,512,512] with
    1 = fill, output float32 [1,3,512,512] in 0..255.

    WHY THIS SPLIT (14.11.2026). The first copy (10.11.2026, 37 MB) kept
    the large layers as int4 and the rest as int8, „no difference to the
    eye" on four holes. Christian then saw one, in a large area: other
    colour values than the full model's. Measured on 16 large holes in two
    of his pictures, the fill's mean colour against the fp32 model's, in
    tone values, on average / at the worst:
        large int4, rest int8   37 MB   2.70 / 7.82     (the first copy)
        large int8, rest int8   59 MB   2.06 / 5.78
        large int4, rest fp16   45 MB   1.69 / 5.48
        large fp16, rest int8   98 MB   2.09 / 5.81
        large int8, rest fp16   66 MB   0.20 / 0.56     (this file)
        fp16 throughout        106 MB   0.18 / 0.59
    So the difference came from the small group, and int4 added its own.
    Over 16 mixed holes (spot, blade, large area) this file stays within
    0.33 tone values of the fp32 model on average (58 dB, 44 dB in the
    worst hole; the first copy 37 and 25 dB), and the fine detail of its
    fill is the fp32 model's to within two per cent.

    NO TENSOR OF MORE THAN FOUR DIMENSIONS (14.11.2026): each of the 36
    Fourier units computed its transform with tensors of five — a trailing
    axis of size 1 for matrix-times-vector, an axis of size 2 that stacks
    real and imaginary parts. onnxruntime-web writes WebGPU shaders for
    rank five and more in a way Firefox's WebGPU refuses to compile, and
    the model fell back to the processor there (16 s per hole instead of
    2.4). Three patterns were replaced by the same arithmetic at rank four
    or less; no weight was touched. On the processor the output is
    IDENTICAL to the file before the rewrite (largest difference 0.0); on
    the graphics card, Chromium and Firefox 159 answer the 16 holes alike
    and as the processor does. The idea is the one published with
    othytenk/lama-int4-int8 (its r4 file), the script written anew; it
    stands below mix.py.

ort.webgpu.bundle.min.mjs, ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm
    ONNX Runtime Web 1.31.1, npm package onnxruntime-web, dist/.
    Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. MIT License.

mix.py — how lama_small.onnx was made from lama_fp32.onnx
(Python 3.12, onnx, numpy; python mix.py lama_fp32.onnx out.onnx int8 fp16,
then flat.py on the result)

"""LaMa's convolution weights stored smaller, with a choice per group of layers.

Blockwise integers with one scale per block, or plain half floats (fp16),
chosen per group of layers — written to find out WHICH layers a difference
to the fp32 model comes from, and then used to make the file:
  BIG   the large FFC convolutions (conv l2l/l2g/g2l and the 384x384 1x1) — 170 MB of 204
  REST  everything else — spectral transforms, down/up-sampling, first and last layers
Each group gets one of: int4, int8, int8b16 (blocks of 16), fp16, keep.

usage: python mix.py <in.onnx> <out.onnx> <big> <rest>
"""
import re
import sys

import numpy as np
import onnx
from onnx import TensorProto, helper, numpy_helper

BIG = re.compile(r"conv(l2g|g2l|l2l)\.weight|anon:384x384x1x1")
MIN_VALUES = 4096


def layer_key(name, w):
    return name if "model.generator" in name else "anon:" + "x".join(str(d) for d in w.shape)


def quantize(w, bits, block, half_scales):
    qmax = 7 if bits == 4 else 127
    rows = w.shape[0]; k = int(np.prod(w.shape[1:])); nblocks = -(-k // block)
    padded = np.zeros((rows, nblocks * block), np.float32); padded[:, :k] = w.reshape(rows, k)
    blocks = padded.reshape(rows, nblocks, block)
    scale = np.abs(blocks).max(axis=2) / qmax
    if half_scales: scale = scale.astype(np.float16).astype(np.float32)
    scale[scale == 0] = 1.0
    q = np.clip(np.round(blocks / scale[..., None]), -qmax - 1, qmax).astype(np.int8)
    return q.reshape(rows, nblocks * block)[:, :k], scale, rows, k


def main(src, dst, big, rest):
    model = onnx.load(src); graph = model.graph
    weights = {t.name: t for t in graph.initializer}
    users = {}
    for n in graph.node:
        for i in n.input: users[i] = users.get(i, 0) + 1
    added_inits, added_nodes, replaced = [], [], set()
    for n in graph.node:
        if n.op_type not in ("Conv", "ConvTranspose") or len(n.input) < 2: continue
        name = n.input[1]
        if name not in weights or name in replaced or users.get(name) != 1: continue
        w = numpy_helper.to_array(weights[name]).astype(np.float32)
        if w.ndim != 4 or w.size < MIN_VALUES: continue
        how = big if BIG.search(layer_key(name, w)) else rest
        if how == "keep": continue
        if how == "fp16":
            hname = name + "_h"
            added_inits.append(numpy_helper.from_array(w.astype(np.float16), hname))
            added_nodes.append(helper.make_node("Cast", [hname], [name + "_w"], to=TensorProto.FLOAT, name=name + "_cast_node"))
        else:
            bits = 4 if how == "int4" else 8
            block = {"int4": 32, "int8": 64, "int8b16": 16}[how]
            half = bits == 4
            q, scale, rows, k = quantize(w, bits, block, half)
            qname, sname, shape_name = name + "_q", name + "_s", name + "_shape"
            if bits == 4:
                nib = (q.reshape(-1) & 0x0F).astype(np.uint8)
                if nib.size % 2: nib = np.append(nib, np.uint8(0))
                q_tensor = helper.make_tensor(qname, TensorProto.INT4, [rows, k], vals=(nib[0::2] | (nib[1::2] << 4)).astype(np.uint8).tobytes(), raw=True)
            else:
                q_tensor = numpy_helper.from_array(q, qname)
            added_inits += [q_tensor, numpy_helper.from_array(scale.astype(np.float16 if half else np.float32), sname),
                            numpy_helper.from_array(np.array(w.shape, np.int64), shape_name)]
            out = name + "_dq"
            added_nodes.append(helper.make_node("DequantizeLinear", [qname, sname], [out], axis=1, block_size=block, name=name + "_dq_node"))
            if half:
                added_nodes.append(helper.make_node("Cast", [out], [out + "_f32"], to=TensorProto.FLOAT, name=name + "_cast_node")); out += "_f32"
            added_nodes.append(helper.make_node("Reshape", [out, shape_name], [name + "_w"], name=name + "_reshape_node"))
        n.input[1] = name + "_w"
        replaced.add(name)
    kept = [t for t in graph.initializer if t.name not in replaced]
    del graph.initializer[:]; graph.initializer.extend(kept + added_inits)
    nodes = list(graph.node); del graph.node[:]; graph.node.extend(added_nodes + nodes)
    for o in model.opset_import:
        if o.domain in ("", "ai.onnx"): o.version = max(o.version, 21)
    onnx.save(model, dst)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(*sys.argv[1:5])


-------------------------------------------------------------------------
flat.py — how the five-dimensional steps were taken out of it
(Python 3.12, onnx, numpy; python flat.py out.onnx lama_small.onnx)

"""LaMa without tensors of more than four dimensions — own implementation.

WHY. Each of LaMa's 36 Fourier units computes its transform with tensors of
five dimensions: a trailing axis of size 1 for matrix-times-vector, and an
axis of size 2 that stacks real and imaginary parts. onnxruntime-web writes
WebGPU shaders for tensors of rank five and more in a way Firefox's WebGPU
refuses to compile, and the model then falls back to the processor there.

WHAT. Three patterns are replaced by the same arithmetic at rank four or less.
No weight is touched, no value changes beyond float rounding:

  A  Squeeze(Sub|Add(MatMul(M, Unsqueeze(X, -1)), ...), -1)
       ->  Sub|Add(MatMul(X, transpose(M)), ...)
     M (K x W) times the column vectors of X is X's row vectors times M^T.

  B  Unsqueeze(R, -1), Unsqueeze(I, -1) -> Concat(-1) -> Transpose(0,1,4,2,3)
     -> Reshape(shape4), with Shape() taken of the 5-D tensor on the way
       ->  Reshape(R, [0,0,-1]), Reshape(I, [0,0,-1]) -> Concat(axis 2)
           -> Reshape(shape4); the 5-D shape is put together from Shape(R).
     Per channel: all of the real part, then all of the imaginary — the
     same order the transposed stack has when flattened.

  C  Reshape(X, [B,C,2,H,W]) -> Transpose(0,1,3,4,2) -> Gather(axis 4, 0|1)
       ->  Reshape(X, [B,-1,2*H*W]) -> Split in two along axis 2
           -> Reshape(each, [B,C,H,W]).

Afterwards every node whose outputs nobody reads is dropped, and the script
refuses to write a file in which shape inference still finds rank five.

usage: python flat.py <in.onnx> <out.onnx>
"""
import sys

import numpy as np
import onnx
from onnx import TensorProto, helper, numpy_helper, shape_inference


def ranks(model):
    inf = shape_inference.infer_shapes(model)
    out = {}
    for vi in list(inf.graph.value_info) + list(inf.graph.input) + list(inf.graph.output):
        out[vi.name] = len(vi.type.tensor_type.shape.dim)
    return out


def main(src: str, dst: str) -> None:
    model = onnx.load(src)
    g = model.graph
    rank = ranks(model)
    nodes = list(g.node)
    producer = {o: n for n in nodes for o in n.output}
    consumers: dict[str, list] = {}
    for n in nodes:
        for i in n.input:
            consumers.setdefault(i, []).append(n)
    inits = {t.name: t for t in g.initializer}

    def const(name):
        """The value of a constant input — an initializer or a Constant node's."""
        if name in inits:
            return numpy_helper.to_array(inits[name])
        n = producer.get(name)
        if n is not None and n.op_type == "Constant":
            for a in n.attribute:
                if a.name == "value":
                    return numpy_helper.to_array(a.t)
                if a.name == "value_int":
                    return np.array(a.i)
                if a.name == "value_ints":
                    return np.array(list(a.ints))
        raise ValueError("not a constant: " + name)

    def attr(n, name, default=None):
        for a in n.attribute:
            if a.name == name:
                return list(a.ints) if a.type == onnx.AttributeProto.INTS else a.i
        return default

    def last_axis(n):
        axes = const(n.input[1]).reshape(-1).tolist()
        return axes in ([-1], [4])

    new_nodes: dict[int, list] = {}      # id(old node) -> nodes that stand in its place
    gone: set[int] = set()
    new_inits = []
    serial = [0]

    def fresh(stem):
        serial[0] += 1
        return f"r4_{stem}_{serial[0]}"

    def i64(values, stem):
        name = fresh(stem)
        new_inits.append(numpy_helper.from_array(np.array(values, np.int64), name))
        return name

    rename: dict[str, str] = {}          # a Squeeze's output -> what it squeezed

    tally = {"A": 0, "B": 0, "C": 0}

    # ---- A: matrix times column vectors ---------------------------------
    transposed: dict[str, tuple] = {}
    for n in nodes:
        if n.op_type != "MatMul" or rank.get(n.output[0], 0) < 5:
            continue
        un = producer.get(n.input[1])
        assert un is not None and un.op_type == "Unsqueeze" and last_axis(un), "MatMul of rank 5 not of pattern A"
        assert rank[n.input[0]] == 2 and rank[un.input[0]] == 4
        m = n.input[0]
        made = []
        if m not in transposed:
            t = fresh("mt")
            transposed[m] = (t, helper.make_node("Transpose", [m], [t], perm=[1, 0], name=t))
            made.append(transposed[m][1])
        made.append(helper.make_node("MatMul", [un.input[0], transposed[m][0]], [n.output[0]], name=n.name + "_r4"))
        new_nodes[id(n)] = made
        gone.add(id(n))
        tally["A"] += 1
    for n in nodes:
        if n.op_type == "Squeeze" and rank.get(n.input[0], 0) >= 5:
            assert last_axis(n) and producer[n.input[0]].op_type in ("Sub", "Add")
            rename[n.output[0]] = n.input[0]
            gone.add(id(n))

    # ---- B: real and imaginary stacked into the channels -----------------
    for n in nodes:
        if n.op_type != "Concat" or rank.get(n.output[0], 0) < 5:
            continue
        assert attr(n, "axis") in (-1, 4) and len(n.input) == 2
        parts = []
        for i in n.input:
            un = producer[i]
            assert un.op_type == "Unsqueeze" and last_axis(un) and rank[un.input[0]] == 4
            parts.append(un.input[0])
        (tr,) = consumers[n.output[0]]
        assert tr.op_type == "Transpose" and attr(tr, "perm") == [0, 1, 4, 2, 3]
        # The 5-D tensor's shape, wherever it was asked for: [B, C, 2, H, W] out of Shape(R).
        # It stands where the Concat stood — before everything that reads it.
        shape_r = fresh("shape_r")
        five = fresh("shape5")
        head, tail = fresh("bc"), fresh("hw")
        new_nodes[id(n)] = [
            helper.make_node("Shape", [parts[0]], [shape_r], name=shape_r),
            helper.make_node("Slice", [shape_r, i64([0], "s"), i64([2], "e"), i64([0], "ax")], [head], name=head),
            helper.make_node("Slice", [shape_r, i64([2], "s"), i64([4], "e"), i64([0], "ax")], [tail], name=tail),
            helper.make_node("Concat", [head, i64([2], "two"), tail], [five], axis=0, name=five),
        ]
        reshape = None
        for c in consumers[tr.output[0]]:
            if c.op_type == "Shape":
                rename[c.output[0]] = five
                gone.add(id(c))
            else:
                assert c.op_type == "Reshape" and reshape is None
                reshape = c
        assert reshape is not None
        flat3 = i64([0, 0, -1], "flat")
        r3, i3, cat = fresh("re"), fresh("im"), fresh("cat")
        made = [
            helper.make_node("Reshape", [parts[0], flat3], [r3], name=r3),
            helper.make_node("Reshape", [parts[1], flat3], [i3], name=i3),
            helper.make_node("Concat", [r3, i3], [cat], axis=2, name=cat),
            helper.make_node("Reshape", [cat, reshape.input[1]], [reshape.output[0]], name=reshape.name + "_r4"),
        ]
        # In the place of the Reshape: its shape input is computed by then.
        new_nodes[id(reshape)] = made
        gone.update({id(n), id(tr), id(reshape)})
        tally["B"] += 1

    # ---- C: the channels split back into real and imaginary --------------
    for n in nodes:
        if n.op_type != "Reshape" or rank.get(n.output[0], 0) < 5:
            continue
        (tr,) = consumers[n.output[0]]
        assert tr.op_type == "Transpose" and attr(tr, "perm") == [0, 1, 3, 4, 2]
        gathers = consumers[tr.output[0]]
        assert len(gathers) == 2 and all(x.op_type == "Gather" and attr(x, "axis") in (4, -1) for x in gathers)
        by_part = {int(const(x.input[1])): x for x in gathers}
        assert set(by_part) == {0, 1}
        s5 = n.input[1]
        # The channel count in s5 may be -1 (left to the Reshape), so it is not
        # read from there: the picture's size H, W is, and the rest follows.
        tail, area, twice, shape3, shape4 = fresh("hw"), fresh("area"), fresh("twice"), fresh("shape3"), fresh("shape4")
        x3, re3, im3, shape_x3, head = fresh("x3"), fresh("re3"), fresh("im3"), fresh("shape_x3"), fresh("bc")
        made = [
            helper.make_node("Slice", [s5, i64([3], "s"), i64([5], "e"), i64([0], "ax")], [tail], name=tail),
            helper.make_node("ReduceProd", [tail], [area], keepdims=1, name=area),
            helper.make_node("Mul", [area, i64([2], "two")], [twice], name=twice),
            helper.make_node("Concat", [i64([0], "same"), i64([-1], "rest"), twice], [shape3], axis=0, name=shape3),
            helper.make_node("Reshape", [n.input[0], shape3], [x3], name=x3),
            helper.make_node("Split", [x3], [re3, im3], axis=2, num_outputs=2, name=fresh("split")),
            helper.make_node("Shape", [x3], [shape_x3], name=shape_x3),
            helper.make_node("Slice", [shape_x3, i64([0], "s"), i64([2], "e"), i64([0], "ax")], [head], name=head),
            helper.make_node("Concat", [head, tail], [shape4], axis=0, name=shape4),
            helper.make_node("Reshape", [re3, shape4], [by_part[0].output[0]], name=by_part[0].name + "_r4"),
            helper.make_node("Reshape", [im3, shape4], [by_part[1].output[0]], name=by_part[1].name + "_r4"),
        ]
        new_nodes[id(n)] = made
        gone.update({id(n), id(tr), id(by_part[0]), id(by_part[1])})
        tally["C"] += 1

    # ---- the graph put together again ------------------------------------
    def through(name):
        while name in rename:
            name = rename[name]
        return name

    out_nodes = []
    for n in nodes:
        if id(n) in new_nodes:
            out_nodes += new_nodes[id(n)]
        if id(n) not in gone:
            out_nodes.append(n)
    for n in out_nodes:
        for k, i in enumerate(n.input):
            n.input[k] = through(i)
    # Only what leads to an output stays.
    needed = {o.name for o in g.output}
    kept = []
    for n in reversed(out_nodes):
        if any(o in needed for o in n.output):
            kept.append(n)
            needed.update(i for i in n.input if i)
    kept.reverse()
    del g.node[:]
    g.node.extend(kept)
    old_inits = [t for t in g.initializer if t.name in needed]
    del g.initializer[:]
    g.initializer.extend(old_inits + [t for t in new_inits if t.name in needed])
    del g.value_info[:]

    onnx.checker.check_model(model)
    left = [name for name, r in ranks(model).items() if r >= 5]
    assert not left, f"{len(left)} tensors of rank five remain, e.g. {left[:3]}"
    onnx.save(model, dst)
    print(f"patterns: {tally}, nodes {len(nodes)} -> {len(kept)}, no tensor above rank 4")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
